Applecross: Where Britain Gets Alpine

Applecross is a remote peninsula on Scotland's west coast, reached by the legendary Bealach na Bà — Britain's most spectacular mountain pass. The combination of an extraordinary road, a beautiful village, stunning views across to Skye, and genuine remoteness makes Applecross one of the UK's most rewarding motorcycle destinations.

The Bealach na Bà

The Bealach na Bà (Pass of the Cattle) rises from sea level at Kishorn to 626 metres in just a few miles. The road features Alpine-style hairpin bends, 20% gradients, cattle grids, and increasingly vertiginous views as you climb. The summit cairn marks the highest point, and the views back east towards the Torridon mountains are extraordinary.

The descent towards Applecross is equally dramatic — the road drops steeply with views across the Inner Sound to Raasay and Skye. On clear days, the Outer Hebrides are visible on the western horizon.

Riding the Bealach

  • Best direction: East to west (climbing from Kishorn) for the most dramatic ascent and the Skye views on the descent
  • Surface: Tarmac is generally good but can have loose gravel on bends. Cattle grids are slippery when wet
  • Width: Single-track with passing places throughout. Be prepared to reverse to passing places for oncoming vehicles
  • Gradient: Up to 20% with hairpin bends. First or second gear for much of the climb
  • Warning signs: The road is not recommended for learner drivers, but experienced motorcyclists shouldn't be deterred
The Bealach na Bà is the single greatest motorcycle road in Britain. Nothing else comes close for the combination of drama, difficulty, and reward. Every British motorcyclist should ride it at least once.

Applecross Village

Applecross village is a small, scattered community on the western shore of the peninsula. The Applecross Inn is famous across the Highlands for its seafood — hand-dived scallops, Applecross Bay prawns, and local venison. The walled garden at Applecross House is open to visitors and the beach offers views across to Skye that could keep you staring for hours.

The Coast Road

The alternative route to Applecross is the coast road from Shieldaig, running along the northern shore of the peninsula. This single-track road hugs the coastline through tiny settlements like Kenmore and Toscaig. It's slower and less dramatic than the Bealach, but the coastal views are beautiful and the sense of remoteness is profound.

Practical Information

There is no fuel station in Applecross. The nearest fuel is at Kishorn, Lochcarron, or Shieldaig — fill up before crossing the Bealach. The Applecross Inn serves food and has rooms. The Applecross Campsite is popular with motorcyclists and offers stunning sea views. Mobile phone signal is unreliable throughout the peninsula. The Bealach na Bà can be closed in winter snow — check conditions before attempting the crossing from November to March. faq.q: Which direction should I ride the Bealach na Ba?
faq.a: Ride east to west, climbing from Kishorn, for the most dramatic ascent and the finest reward. The descent towards Applecross opens up views across the Inner Sound to Raasay and Skye, and on clear days the Outer Hebrides appear on the western horizon. It is the single greatest motorcycle road in Britain.

No. There is no fuel station in Applecross, so fill up at Kishorn, Lochcarron or Shieldaig before crossing the Bealach na Ba. Mobile phone signal is also unreliable throughout the peninsula, so plan ahead and do not rely on your phone for navigation or emergencies.

faq.q: Where can I eat and stay in Applecross?
faq.a: The Applecross Inn is famous across the Highlands for its seafood, including hand-dived scallops, Applecross Bay prawns and local venison, and it has rooms. The Applecross Campsite is popular with motorcyclists and offers stunning sea views across to Skye.

faq.q: Is there an alternative route to Applecross?
faq.a: Yes. The coast road from Shieldaig runs along the northern shore of the peninsula through tiny settlements like Kenmore and Toscaig. It is slower and less dramatic than the Bealach, but the coastal views are beautiful and the sense of remoteness is profound. It is also the sensible option when the pass is closed by snow.

faq.q: Can I ride the Bealach na Ba in winter?
faq.a: Take great care. The Bealach na Ba can be closed by winter snow, so check conditions before attempting the crossing between November and March. Cattle grids on the pass become slippery when wet, and loose gravel can gather on the bends at any time of year.
